These properties are often used together, or via the `flex`shorthand property. ![csstricks]![CSS-Tricks](data:image/png;base64,)CSS-Tricks +2`flex-grow`-   **Purpose:** Specifies how much a flex item will **grow** relative to other items to fill available *positive* free space along the main axis of the container.-   **Value:** A unitless number (default is `0`). A higher number means the item takes up a greater proportion of the remaining space.-   **Behavior:** If all items have `flex-grow: 1`, the extra space is distributed evenly, making them equal in size if their initial sizes were the same.![YouTube](data:image/png;base64,)`flex-shrink`-   **Purpose:** Specifies how much a flex item will **shrink** relative to other items if the combined size of all items is too large for the container (i.e., when *negative* free space is distributed).-   **Value:** A unitless number (default is `1`), which determines the item's "shrink factor".-   **Behavior:**    -   `flex-shrink: 1` (default) allows the item to shrink proportionally to the other items to fit inside the container.    -   `flex-shrink: 0` prevents the item from shrinking below its initial size. ![MDN Web Docs](data:image/png;base64,)MDN Web Docs +5`flex-wrap`-   **Purpose:** Controls whether flex items are forced onto a single line or allowed to **wrap** onto multiple lines if they overflow the container.-   **Values:**    -   `nowrap` (default): All items stay on a single line and may shrink (if `flex-shrink` allows) to fit.    -   `wrap`: Items wrap onto new lines from top to bottom when there isn't enough space to fit them all on one line.    -   `wrap-reverse`: Items wrap onto multiple lines from bottom to top.-   **Behavior:** When items wrap, each line acts as its own separate flex container for space distribution. ^CoderPad^+^3 ![CoderPad]Shorthand `flex` PropertyThe recommended way to use these properties is with the `flex` shorthand: css```css.item {  flex: flex-grow flex-shrink flex-basis;}```-   `flex: 1` is equivalent to `flex: 1 1 0` (grow, shrink, and basis of 0).-   `flex: auto` is equivalent to `flex: 1 1 auto`(full flexibility with an automatic initial size).-   `flex: initial` is equivalent to `flex: 0 1 auto` (doesn't grow, can shrink, automatic initial size).-   `flex: none` is equivalent to `flex: 0 0 auto`(inflexible, no growing or shrinking, automatic initial size). -   ![YouTube](data:image/png;base64,)YouTube +2[](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Flexible_box_layout/Controlling_flex_item_ratios#:~:text=The%20flex%2Dshrink%20property%20specifies,them%20to%20overflow%20the%20container.)Controlling ratios of flex items along the main axis - A higher number means the item takes up a greater proportion of the remaining space.• Behavior: If all items have , the extra space is distributed evenly, making them equal in size if their initial sizes were the same. [^3][^18][^19][^3][^18][^19]The recommended way to use these properties is with the `flex` shorthand: css```css.item {  flex: flex-grow flex-shrink flex-basis;}```-   `flex: 1` is equivalent to `flex: 1 1 0` (grow, shrink, and basis of 0).-   `flex: auto` is equivalent to `flex: 1 1 auto`(full flexibility with an automatic initial size).-   `flex: initial` is equivalent to `flex: 0 1 auto` (doesn't grow, can shrink, automatic initial size).-   `flex: none` is equivalent to `flex: 0 0 auto`(inflexible, no growing or shrinking, automatic initial
